title: Shortest Palindrome
description:
# Shortest Palindrome

Given a string `s`, add characters only to the front of `s` so that the final string is a palindrome.

Return the shortest palindrome that can be obtained this way.

A palindrome reads the same forward and backward, such as `"aba"` or `"aa"`. A single character is also a palindrome.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "aacecaaa"
**Output:** "aaacecaaa"

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "abcd"
**Output:** "dcbabcd"

## Important Details

Return `s` unchanged if it is already a palindrome. An empty input returns an empty string. Do not remove or reorder original characters or insert characters within them.

## Constraints:

* `0 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4`
* `s` consists of lowercase English letters only.

solutions.name: KMP Failure Function
solutions.description:
## Approach

Reverse the string and build `s + separator + reverse(s)`, where the separator is a character that cannot appear in `s`. Compute the KMP failure function on that combined string. The final failure value is the length of the longest prefix of `s` that also matches a suffix of `reverse(s)`, which is exactly the longest palindromic prefix of `s`.

## Key Insight

A prefix of `s` is a palindrome exactly when it equals its own reverse. In `s + separator + reverse(s)`, the final KMP border can only connect the beginning of `s` with the end of `reverse(s)`, so it identifies the longest palindromic prefix without checking every prefix separately.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Z-Function Border Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build the same combined string `s + separator + reverse(s)`, but compute the Z-function instead of the KMP failure function. For every position inside the reversed half, `z[i]` tells how many characters from the start of `s` match there. If `i + z[i]` reaches the end of the combined string, that match aligns a prefix of `s` with the corresponding reversed prefix, so it is a palindromic prefix candidate.

## Key Insight

The Z-function reports prefix matches starting at every position. A match that reaches the very end of the reversed half means the original prefix and its reverse line up completely, so the matched length is a valid palindromic prefix.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Manacher Prefix Radius
solutions.description:
## Approach

Run Manacher's algorithm on a transformed string with separators between every character. Each radius describes a palindrome around one center. Among the palindromes whose left boundary touches the beginning of `s`, take the largest original length; that is the longest palindromic prefix. Reverse the remaining suffix and prepend it.

## Key Insight

Manacher normally finds palindromes centered anywhere. Restricting the candidates to radii that start at the first transformed character converts it into a longest-palindromic-prefix finder while keeping the linear-time expansion guarantees.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Check Palindrome Prefixes
solutions.description:
## Approach

Try prefix lengths from longest to shortest. For each length, use two pointers to test whether `s[0..len)` is a palindrome. The first successful prefix is the longest palindromic prefix, so reverse the suffix after it and prepend that reversed suffix to the original string.

## Key Insight

This baseline states the core reduction directly: only the longest palindromic prefix matters. It is not the optimal method for the full constraint, but it is useful as a reference point for why KMP, Z-function, and Manacher all search for the same prefix more efficiently.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
